result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_spectrum()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23827-L23956){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_spectrum( which="largest", k=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the spectrum (eigenvalues and eigenvectors) of the graph's adjacency matrix. The spectrum reveals important structural properties including connectivity, bipartiteness, and graph regularity. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [which]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["largest"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which eigenvalues to compute: - `"all"`: All `n` eigenvalues (`O(n³)`, recommended for `n < 100`) - `"largest"`: Largest k eigenvalues (default `k=6`) - `"smallest"`: Smallest k eigenvalues [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of eigenvalues to compute for "largest"/"smallest". Default is `min(6, n-1)` where `n` is the number of nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary with keys: - `"values"`: List of eigenvalues (sorted descending) - `"vectors"`: List of eigenvectors (each as list of floats) - `"spectral_gap"`: λ₁ - λ₂ (difference between two largest eigenvalues) ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is empty or eigenvalue computation fails. ::: ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - spectral clustering: community detection via eigenvectors - graph embedding: represent nodes using eigenvector coordinates - bipartite detection: check if spectrum is symmetric about `0` - random walk analysis: eigenvalues determine mixing time - graph comparison: compare spectral distributions ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Spectral Properties**: - **Spectral radius**: `ρ(A) = max|λᵢ|` - always equals largest eigenvalue for undirected graphs - bounded by max degree: `ρ(A) ≤ Δ(G)` - for regular graphs: `ρ(A) = degree` - **Spectral gap**: `λ₁ - λ₂` - measures connectivity and expansion - large gap -> well-connected graph - small gap -> bottlenecks or clusters - zero gap -> disconnected graph - **Trace**: `Σλᵢ = 0` (sum of eigenvalues equals zero for undirected) - **Number of spanning trees**: Related to Laplacian eigenvalues **Special Graph Spectra**: - complete graph K_n: {n-1, -1, -1, ..., -1} - cycle C_n: {2cos(2πk/n) | k=0,...,n-1} - path P_n: {2cos(πk/(n+1)) | k=1,...,n} - star S_n: {√(n-1), 0, ..., 0, -√(n-1)} **Computational Complexity**: - `which="all"`: `O(n³)` using dense eigendecomposition - `which="largest"/"smallest"`: `O(kn²)` using iterative methods - Recommended: Use `k < 10` for large graphs (`n > 1000`) ## Examples {.doc-examples} **Spectral Analysis of Complete Graph** A complete graph `K_5` has a very distinctive spectrum: one large eigenvalue of `n-1` and the rest equal to `-1`, which produces a large spectral gap: ::: {#56fccffc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(5): g.add_node(f"v{i}") for i in range(5): for j in range(i+1, 5): g.add_edge(f"v{i}", f"v{j}") spec = g.get_spectrum(which="all") # Returns [4.0, -1.0, -1.0, -1.0, -1.0] spec['values'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [4.000000000000002, -0.9999999999999996, -1.0, -1.0, -1.0] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#9d4a08cb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 5.0 (largest minus second-largest eigenvalue) spec['spectral_gap'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5.000000000000002 ``` ::: ::: **Detecting Bipartite Structure** A bipartite graph's spectrum is symmetric around zero -- the largest and smallest eigenvalues are mirror images of each other: ::: {#d41f45ff .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) # Left partition: A, B; right partition: X, Y, Z for node in ["A", "B", "X", "Y", "Z"]: g.add_node(node) g.add_edge("A", "X") g.add_edge("A", "Y") g.add_edge("B", "Y") g.add_edge("B", "Z") spec = g.get_spectrum(which="all") values = spec['values'] # Returns True: the spectrum is symmetric about zero, a signature of bipartiteness abs(values[0] + values[-1]) < 0.01 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
